title: Pacific Fusion secures key licence for New Mexico campus
html:
The licence authorises Pacific Fusion to safely possess and use tritium for fusion at its Research and Manufacturing Campus. The company noted that the small amounts of tritium used will be contained in a closed system, and any waste will be safely disposed of at a licensed facility outside the state.

This is the first radioactive materials licence the New Mexico Environment Department (NMED) has ever issued to a private fusion company, Pacific Fusion said, adding that it will continue working closely with NMED as construction progresses.

California-headquartered Pacific Fusion broken ground in August for its USD1 billion Research and Manufacturing Campus in Albuquerque. The campus at Mesa del Sol will house the company's Demonstration System, designed to achieve net facility gain by 2030, producing more energy from fusion than the total energy initially stored in the machine.

The Demonstration System will also produce bursts of high-energy fusion output exceeding 100 megajoules, making it the only "high-yield" fusion facility under construction in the USA. High-yield fusion refers to the capability to create certain conditions relevant to national security research, providing a long-sought platform for the science required to maintain the US nuclear stockpile without explosive nuclear testing.

The company said the approval of its radioactive materials licence "demonstrates just how quickly fusion is moving in New Mexico. The approval comes a year after Pacific Fusion announced its decision to build in the state and reflects close collaboration between the company and state officials to advance a first-of-a-kind energy and advanced manufacturing project while maintaining rigorous safety and environmental standards".

"Leaders across the state have demonstrated what's possible when government and industry work hand in hand to deploy new energy technologies," said Carrie von Muench, co-founder and Chief Operating Officer of Pacific Fusion. "This licence is an essential milestone on our path to putting clean fusion energy on the grid, and we're grateful to the New Mexico Environment Department for their commitment to helping us move quickly and responsibly. We're proud to be building the future of fusion energy here in New Mexico."

"New Mexico is proving that we can lead the clean energy transition while creating good-paying jobs and building the industries of the future," said New Mexico Environment Secretary James Kenney. "Our Energy Transition Act set ambitious goals for a zero-carbon electricity future, and innovations like fusion could play an important role in helping us achieve them. Today's milestone is another clear step forward, demonstrating that New Mexico has the talent, infrastructure and commitment to lead the next generation of clean energy innovation while ensuring protections for public health and the environment."

Pacific Fusion was founded in 2023 and is developing a pulser-driven inertial fusion system using modular, mass-manufacturable components made of readily available materials. Its technology advances decades of US government investment at national laboratories, including Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Sandia National Laboratories, and Los Alamos National Laboratory.
summary: The New Mexico Environment Department has approved the radioactive materials licence for pulsed magnetic fusion system developer Pacific Fusion's Research and Manufacturing Campus in Albuquerque, enabling the company to operate a fusion machine.
